eintraege.text:
Win 55 % of your 0.5 % scalps and you still lose money.

Target 0.5 %, stop 0.5 %, and 0.1 % in fees and slippage on every round trip. A win nets +0.4 %, a loss costs −0.6 %. Break-even is now 60 % winners, and at 55 % every trade loses 0.05 % on average.

The same costs on a 2 % trade need only 52.5 %. The tighter the trade, the bigger the share costs take.

eintraege.titel: On 2x margin, a 33 % drop takes 67 % of your money.
eintraege.text:
On 2x margin, a 33 % drop takes 67 % of your money.

$10,000 of your own and $10,000 borrowed buys $20,000 of stock. The stock falls a third: the position is worth $13,333 and you still owe $10,000. Your part is $3,333. At a 25 % maintenance requirement that is the margin call, and the broker can sell without asking you first.

At −50 % your part is zero. The loan stays exactly where it is.

Send this to the friend who calls margin "free buying power".

Have you ever had a margin call? 👇

eintraege.titel: Sell at a $2,000 loss, buy back within 30 days, and that deduction is gone for this year.
eintraege.text:
Sell at a $2,000 loss, buy back within 30 days, and that deduction is gone for this year.

That is the US wash sale rule: 30 days before and 30 days after, same or substantially identical stock. The loss moves into the cost basis of the new shares, and you get it back when you finally sell those.

20 round trips in December on one ticker and your tax software finds 20 wash sales in January. Your broker reports them on the 1099-B.
